hero.title: Trust that no nation
hero.subtitle: Genesis Mesh is portable trust infrastructure for sovereign systems - cryptographic identity, recognition treaties, and revocable authority that work the same for the 190 countries still searching for digital sovereignty, and for the three that already have it.

meta.auditDesc: so no one takes your word

stakes.label: The Stakes
stakes.title: Digital sovereignty is now a question of national survival - and there is no treaty layer for machines.
stakes.subtitle: States sign treaties. Digital systems have no equivalent. When an AI agent of one nation meets the infrastructure of another, the question - who vouches for this entity, under whose rules, and can that trust be withdrawn - is a diplomatic question that today has no protocol answer. Genesis Mesh is that answer.
stakes.notLine: Not a blockchain. Not a VPN. Not a service mesh. Not an agent framework. Not a marketplace. The treaty layer for machines.

stats.oneDesc: Nations still searching for a sovereignty formula
stats.twoDesc: Powers that already own their stack
stats.threeDesc: Protocol that serves both - without picking a side

powers.label: The Three Powers
powers.title: Sovereign powers don't need independence. They need interoperation without subordination.
powers.subtitle: The value flips, but it doesn't disappear. No allied capital accepts another's root of trust - so recognition must travel as signed, scoped, revocable treaties between equals.

cn.title: Prove non-control, technically.
cn.desc: Every infrastructure export meets the same objection: your equipment means your control. Verifiable, operator-owned, revocable trust is the technical answer to that political objection.
benefits: Partner nations audit and revoke without trusting anyone's word
Cross-recognition with Western sovereigns - neither side holds the other's keys
Chinese-Western integration under a single governance model

us.title: Allies won't take your root.
us.desc: Five Eyes, NATO, EU partners: none will subordinate to a US-controlled trust anchor. Recognition treaties let each ally stay sovereign while trust still flows.
benefits: Hyperscalers sell into foreign sovereignty law

kp.title: The paranoid-sovereign test.
kp.desc: A state that trusts nothing external. If a protocol works for the most guarded sovereign on earth - zero dependency, full operator ownership - it works for anyone.

mechanics.label: The Mechanics
mechanics.title: Infrastructure that encodes no politics - only mechanics.
mechanics.subtitle: Most trust infrastructure encodes the politics of whoever runs the root. Genesis Mesh encodes only four operations and leaves the politics to the sovereigns. That is what makes it treaty-grade rather than vendor-grade.

ops.name: Verify
ops.desc: Cryptographic proof of who holds authority - Ed25519 identity, signed genesis blocks, evidence chains.

ops.name: Limit
ops.desc: Scoped, time-bounded delegations. Capability manifests define what each identity may do - nothing more.

ops.name: Revoke
ops.desc: The moment trust breaks, signed revocation propagates across sovereign boundaries - and is honored.

ops.name: Audit
ops.desc: Every decision leaves tamper-evident evidence. No one has to take your word for it.

protocol.label: The Protocol
protocol.title: An open RFC program - standards-shaped, not vendor-shaped.
protocol.subtitle: Three SDK generations shipped (TypeScript, Go, .NET). 1,041 tests. Eight machine-checked Tamarin lemmas. Multi-cloud sovereigns live on Azure, DigitalOcean, Cloudflare, and Akamai/Linode.

stack.title: The Stack
stack.l1: L1 - Protocol Core. Ed25519 identity, signed genesis blocks, enrollment, revocation, routing, audit.
stack.l2: L2 - Sovereign Communities. Independent trust domains. Each controls its own membership, governance, revocation.
stack.l3: L3 - Recognition Network. Treaties between sovereigns. Trust paths and revocation propagation across boundaries.

silicon.label: The Silicon
silicon.title: A sovereign protocol on foreign silicon is theater.
silicon.subtitle: Genesis Mesh verifies authority in software. But software is only as sovereign as the silicon it runs on. TSWI - the Tunisian Sovereign Wafer Initiative - closes the loop: owned interposer IP, owned packaging facility, owned orchestration stack. Commodity chiplets in; sovereign compute out. Solar-powered at the crossroads of three continents, with more than half the compute cost stripped out. Phase one is done.
silicon.conclusion: The protocol governs the logic. Tunisia governs the silicon.

live.label: Live
live.title: Not a promise. A running system.
live.subtitle: One authority model, in production. Not a pilot, and not a reference architecture.

closing.title: Hire the authority.
closing.subtitle: For the 190, it is the shortest path to owning your trust anchors. For the three, it is the only way to interoperate without giving them up.

builders.title: Spin up your own sovereign trust domain.
builders.desc: Read the RFCs, pull the TypeScript / Go / .NET SDKs, and stand up an L2 Sovereign Community on infrastructure you already own.

strategic.title: This conversation does not start with an SDK.
